items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Paul Whiteman was — Paul Whiteman was reasonably popular. But I don’t think that meant quite as much in Europe as it did in the U.S.

ctx.x: Was Paul Whiteman part of that?

Paul Whiteman was — Paul Whiteman was reasonably popular. But I don’t think that meant quite as much in Europe as it did in the U.S. When you consider the ‘30s you’ve got to consider the big influence of radio. I mean what people could hear on radio was so very influential you know. I mean we didn’t have — in England we had English bands playing on the radio, fairly corny most of them. But here, I mean reputations were made I mean Earl Hines at the Grand Terrace in Chicago, he was heard from the midwest west,…
